calls.title: The Atlantic<>GrowthBook - Deep Dive Session
calls.summary:
# MEDDICC Sales Call Summary

Call on [date not specified in transcript] with Jake Heier (GrowthBook Account Executive), Logan Bates (GrowthBook Technical Lead), Sophie Katasi (Atlantic, likely Product/Analytics Lead), Jason Langsner (Atlantic VP of Data), Derek Shin (Atlantic Data Scientist), Alisha Isaacs (Atlantic, attendee from previous call), and Rebecca (Atlantic, attendee status unclear).

## Key Attendees & Authority
Jason Langsner, VP of Data, explicitly stated his role as supporter who would "help to push it through with leadership," signaling budget authority and decision-making influence. Sophie Katasi appeared to lead the Atlantic team's evaluation process. Derek Shin, as a data scientist, represented technical requirements perspective, while Alisha Isaacs provided continuity from previous discussions.

## Quantifiable Outcomes & Metrics
While specific ROI metrics weren't discussed in this deep-dive session, the Atlantic team identified a critical objective: scaling their experimentation program to run more tests over the next 6-12 months. This timeframe established clear measurable goals around test volume and frequency, though specific numerical targets weren't articulated in the available transcript.

## Technical Requirements & Pain Points
Three primary pain points emerged: (1) need for cross-functional testing capabilities across product, engineering, and marketing teams with different requirements; (2) requirement for warehouse-native deployment ensuring data stays within their existing data warehouse infrastructure; (3) demand for transparency and ability to audit underlying SQL queries generating results. Atlantic's established data stack and data warehouse made the warehouse-native approach particularly attractive, addressing security concerns around PII exposure.

## Solution Fit Discussion
GrowthBook's three-component platform—feature flags, experimentation, and product analytics—appeared well-aligned with Atlantic's needs. The warehouse-native architecture resonated strongly, with data flowing to Atlantic's warehouse while GrowthBook maintained read-only access for aggregate analysis only. The open-source, customizable nature addressed flexibility requirements.

## Technical Clarifications
Sophie Katasi raised specific questions about Visual Editor capabilities, particularly regarding mobile versus web limitations. Logan Bates clarified that the Visual Editor operates as a Chrome extension for web-only use currently, with mobile expansion contingent on customer demand. GrowthBook demonstrated traditional A/B testing and multivariant bandit testing capabilities, plus upcoming contextual multivariant bandit functionality.

## Decision Process & Timeline
No explicit decision timeline emerged in this transcript segment, though the deep-dive demo format indicated Atlantic progressed beyond initial exploration. Jason Langsner's presence suggested movement toward evaluation completion, with leadership approval phase anticipated.

## Next Steps
The team proceeded directly into platform demonstration, with Logan Bates walking through Visual Editor workflow and testing capabilities. No specific follow-up meeting dates or deliverables were documented in the provided transcript excerpt.
